Raised on the round 2 .env.example (3f66ef3), which 01d0f33 removed: its line 1 said Copy to .env and adjust, but nothing loads a .env file (the API reads the settings from the process environment, application.properties:L3-L6, DatabaseConfig.java:L23 via todo.db.path; Spring Boot has no dotenv support; Vite reads only web/.env VITE_ variables), and the root .gitignore has no .env entry. Folded by the requester into the NFR-002 AC-1 follow-up change (F-14); it applies when that change restores the file.
findings.suggestion: In the follow-up, say to export the variables in the shell (or pass them on the command line) instead of copying to .env, or add .env to .gitignore if a .env workflow is intended.

findings.message: Harness tooling. A diverged row {requirement NFR-001, projects [firefox]} added beside the met NFR-001 row was refused: register refused (1 problem): - duplicate row NFR-001. The register therefore records no Firefox row; the Firefox divergence stays a PR-listed divergence (F-9, follow-up: run the firefox project in CI on Linux). Turning a met row into diverged to fit it would misstate the register, so it was not done. Also: conformance build --agent validator was refused with: error: --agent and --run-id go together (the agent session that wrote the rows); or leave both out: the hooks record of the calling run names it; the register was built without the flags and names the run from the hook record.
findings.suggestion: Let the register carry a change-level project divergence row (or a projects field on a met row), then record the Firefox divergence there.
